sections.content: Relative clauses add information about a person, thing or place without starting a separate sentence. *Que* is the most common relative pronoun, while *quien* and *donde* are useful for people and places in appropriate contexts.

items.spanish: La amiga que vive al lado siempre nos ayuda cuando tenemos problemas.
items.english: The friend who lives next door always helps us when we have problems.

items.spanish: Conozco a una familia que comparte muchas actividades con sus vecinos.
items.english: I know a family that shares many activities with its neighbours.

items.spanish: El vecino con quien hablamos ayer conoce bien a mi hermano.
items.english: The neighbour with whom we spoke yesterday knows my brother well.

items.spanish: La casa donde nos reuníamos de pequeños ya no existe.
items.english: The house where we used to meet as children no longer exists.

sections.content: The relative clause normally follows the noun it describes. Choose the relative form according to its role in the clause, not simply according to the noun before it.
